strengths: Identifies and addresses the critical 'Jensen's Gap' in physics-constrained diffusion models, which arises from imposing constraints on the posterior mean estimate instead of the actual final sample.

Proposes a simple, training-efficient post-hoc distillation framework (PIDDM) that decouples physical constraint enforcement from the generative diffusion trajectory, enabling high-fidelity one-step generation.

Provides solid theoretical backing via a linearized analysis (Theorems B.1 and B.2) that explains why score-space guidance struggles near the clean endpoint and proves that post-hoc distillation systematically shrinks constraint violations.

Presents an exceptionally comprehensive empirical evaluation across a wide range of PDE benchmarks (Darcy, Poisson, Burgers, Helmholtz, Stokes, Heat, Navier-Stokes, Porous Medium, and Stefan), consistently outperforming strong baselines in both statistical and physical metrics.
weaknesses: The distilled student model is fundamentally bounded by the quality and coverage of the pre-trained teacher model; any calibration issues or lack of diversity in the teacher will propagate to the student.

The physics loss weight (\lambda_train) is highly sensitive to the stiffness of the governing equations, requiring tuning from 10 to 10^6 across different PDEs, which slightly weakens the claim of 'minimal hyperparameter tuning'.

Theorem B.2 indicates a coordinate shrinkage effect proportional to 1/(1+\lambda). While this successfully satisfies constraints, it may risk over-regularizing the generated fields and reducing sample diversity in high-dimensional, complex constraint scenarios.

Inference-time refinement (PIDDM-ref) and optimization-based downstream tasks still require backpropagation through the student network, which introduces non-trivial computational overhead compared to pure feedforward models.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental theoretical limitation of existing physics-informed diffusion models: the 'Jensen's Gap' mismatch, which occurs when non-linear PDE constraints are applied to the posterior mean estimator instead of the final clean sample.
Proposed post-hoc distillation framework (PIDDM) elegantly decouples generative diffusion training from physics constraint enforcement, allowing any standard pre-trained teacher model to be utilized.
Achieves exceptional computational efficiency, supporting fast single-step generation (1 NFE) that outperforms many-step baselines in both physical consistency and sample quality.

Provides extensive empirical validation across nine diverse PDE benchmarks (including Darcy, Poisson, Burgers, Helmholtz, Navier-Stokes) and various downstream tasks (forward, inverse, and reconstruction).

Complemented by a strong theoretical analysis (Appendix B) that rigorously explains why final-sample distillation mitigates the slow convergence issues of score-based models along constrained directions.
weaknesses: The distilled student model is heavily dependent on the quality and coverage of the teacher model; if the teacher fails to capture certain modes of the distribution, the distilled student cannot recover them.

While the computational speedup is impressive, the training cost of the post-hoc distillation phase (requiring teacher trajectory sampling to build the dataset) can still be substantial, which should be explicitly quantified in the main text.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental theoretical limitation in physics-guided diffusion models, namely 'Jensen's Gap', arising from applying non-linear PDE constraints to the posterior mean estimate during the denoising trajectory.

Proposes an elegant and practical solution (PIDDM) that decouples generative learning from constraint enforcement via post-hoc distillation, directly penalizing PDE violations on the final generated samples.

Provides solid theoretical support with a bimodal Mixture of Gaussians (MoG) toy analysis and proofs showing why score-based models fail to learn constrained directions accurately, while the distillation strategy effectively mitigates this.

Demonstrates excellent empirical results across a comprehensive suite of PDE benchmarks (Darcy, Poisson, Burgers, Helmholtz, Navier-Stokes, etc.), consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in both generative quality (MMSE, SMSE) and physical consistency (PDE error), while offering huge speedups (up to 1 NFE).
weaknesses: The method introduces an additional post-hoc distillation training stage. Generating the paired training dataset via the teacher model's ODE trajectories and optimizing the student model with costly PDE residual backpropagation requires notable offline computation compared to zero-shot sampling-time guidance methods.

The performance of the student model is fundamentally bound by the representation capability of the unconstrained teacher model. If the teacher's training data is limited or of low quality, the distillation stage might struggle to recover physical fidelity even with strong PDE regularization.
